newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul says will not tolerate future illegal strikes.
newsitem.headline: Seoul says will not tolerate future illegal strikes.

text.p: South Korean Labour Minister Jin Nyum said on Thursday the government would not tolerate any more illegal strikes over a controversial labour law.

Ministry officials quoted Jin as telling local businessmen that wildcat stoppages had damaged the economy. But Jin did not specify what measures would be taken against strikers or when this would take effect.

"The minister said the workers should stop illegal strikes while a solution is being sought by politicians," Son Khong-ho, a director-general at the ministry, told Reuters. He accompanied Jin at the meeting.
"He said no more illegal activities will be tolerated," Son added.

President Kim Young-sam said on Tuesday that he would suspend arrest warrants outstanding for leaders of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, which led more than three weeks of wildcat stoppages in protest at the law.
But Son said he believed Kim did not mean illegal activities would be allowed in the future.
